Write ONE new file: tests/test_preflight_interrupts.py (pytest) for the existing script scripts/preflight_interrupts.py. Read that script first; do not edit it or any other file.

Import it with: sys.path.insert(0, str(Path(__file__).resolve().parent.parent / "scripts")); import preflight_interrupts as pi

Cover, using tmp_path and monkeypatch to point pi.ROOT, pi.QA_DIR and pi.EVENTS at a fake tree (never the real games/ files, except one test noted below):
1. qa_args: "just qa field" -> ["field"]; "PARLEY_NO_X_INPUT=1 just qa all kind=instant" -> ["all","kind=instant"]; "just qa field && echo done" stops at &&; "just qa-restore" -> None; "echo hi" -> None.
2. parse_run: kind=instant and "--kind instant" set instant; case=X and "--case X" collect cases; no-smoke and --no-smoke clear smoke; "--real games/local/x.toml" is skipped and not taken as the suite.
3. turn_cases: a suite with one instant and one turn case (kind omitted means turn) returns only the turn one; smoke suite is prepended unless no-smoke; case= filters non-smoke suites; "all" reads every suite toml in QA_DIR.
4. unhandled: an event with ruled_out passes; held_by with a proof "path::regex" that matches a file under ROOT passes; held_by whose proof regex doesn't match is reported with "isn't built"; held_by with no proof is reported; an event with neither is reported with "nothing holds it off".
5. main: exit 0 for an instant-only run, exit 0 for a non-qa command, exit 0 when the run has no turn case, exit 1 with the event id in stdout when an event is unhandled (use capsys), exit 0 when every event is handled.
6. One test on the REAL repo files (no monkeypatch): main(["just qa all kind=instant"]) == 0, and main(["just qa-restore"]) == 0.

Run it with: .venv/bin/python -m pytest tests/test_preflight_interrupts.py -q
All tests must pass. Reply with the final pytest summary line only.

Goal: QA bench turn cases must never meet a papal election. The Pope dies of old age; EOP lets a character's age be written. Build a bench "quiet world" step that makes the Pope young (age 45) right after EVERY bench save load, before any turn plays, and logs his age.

Work on a new git branch `feat/young-pope` in this repo (main checkout, not a worktree). Do NOT run the game, `just qa`, `just play`, or anything touching the live game; do not push.

Steps:
1. Read how the bench loads its save: parley/qa/runner.py (load_bench_save / _load_bench, the M.qa.load call) and the QA Lua helpers in lua/parley_bridge.lua (search `M.qa.`). Find how the bridge identifies the Pope / papal faction (search lua/parley_bridge.lua and docs for papal, pope, "papal_states") and the EOP API for a character's age: the indexed EOP docs live at /home/bill/.code-index/local-eopScripts-de182036/LuaDocs.lua (search for "age"). Use only API that exists there; cite the line in a comment.
2. Add Lua `M.qa.quiet()` in lua/parley_bridge.lua: find the Pope character (papal faction leader), set age to 45 if older, and return a string like "pope=<name> age=<old>-><new>" (or "pope=none" when there is no Pope). Never raise.
3. Call it from the runner right after every bench load (fresh-isolation reloads included), log the returned line to the run report / bridge log the way neighbouring steps log, and make a load whose quiet() call errors fail loudly (not silently continue).
4. Unit tests in tests/ using the existing fake-bridge / runner test patterns (find them in tests/test_qa_runner.py) proving quiet() is called after each load and its line is recorded, and a failing call is reported.
5. In games/interrupts.toml, under [events.papal_election] add:
   held_by = "M.qa.quiet() makes the Pope 45 after every bench load (old-age death is the election cause)"
   proof = ["lua/parley_bridge.lua::function M\\.qa\\.quiet", "parley/qa/runner.py::<a regex matching your runner call>"]
   and keep the existing `what`/`note` lines.
6. Run: .venv/bin/python -m pytest -q -p no:warnings  — the whole suite must pass. Also run: python3 scripts/preflight_interrupts.py "just qa field" and report its output (papal_election must no longer be listed).
7. Commit on the branch with a clear message ending with the line: Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

Reply with: branch name, commit hash, the pytest summary line, the preflight output, and the exact EOP API you used with its LuaDocs.lua line number.

Write ONE new file: tests/test_session_edit_guard.py (pytest) for the existing scripts/session_edit_guard.py. Read that script first. Do not edit any other file. Do not run git. Only touch paths inside this repo and pytest's tmp_path.

Import: sys.path.insert(0, str(Path(__file__).resolve().parent.parent / "scripts")); import session_edit_guard as g

Build a FAKE /proc and socket dir under tmp_path (never the real /proc or /run): for a fake pid N create proc/N/status containing "PPid:\t<parent>\n", proc/N/cmdline as b"claude\0--flag\0" (or b"python3\0" for a non-claude process), and proc/N/cwd as a symlink (os.symlink) to a directory; create socks/N.sock as an empty file. Fake checkouts are tmp dirs containing a ".git" directory (or a ".git" FILE for a worktree).

Call g.decide(data, sock_dir, proc, me) and g.main(io.StringIO(json), sock_dir=..., proc=..., me=...) with me = a fake pid whose PPid chain leads to this session's fake claude pid.

Cases (one test each):
1. Edit into another checkout where a live claude session's cwd is inside it -> deny reason mentions that checkout and the pid.
2. Edit into this session's own checkout while another session also works there -> allowed (None).
3. Edit into another checkout with no live session -> allowed.
4. The hook's own ancestor claude pid is never counted as another session (its socket exists, its cwd is the target checkout, target is a different checkout from data["cwd"]... i.e. only ancestors -> allowed).
5. A socket whose pid's cmdline argv0 is not claude (pid reuse) -> ignored -> allowed.
6. A socket whose /proc entry is missing (dead session) -> ignored.
7. A worktree (.git file) nested inside a repo is its own checkout: session in the outer repo, edit inside the worktree -> allowed; and session in the worktree, edit in the outer repo from a third checkout -> only the outer session matters.
8. The override marker .claude/allow-cross-session-edits in the target checkout -> allowed.
9. A relative file_path is resolved against data["cwd"].
10. NotebookEdit's notebook_path is checked like file_path.
11. main() prints JSON with hookSpecificOutput.permissionDecision == "deny" on a deny (capsys), prints nothing and returns 0 on allow, and returns 0 with no output for invalid JSON input.
12. Missing socket dir -> no sessions -> allowed.
Monkeypatch g.LOG to a path under tmp_path so no real log is written.

Run: .venv/bin/python -m pytest tests/test_session_edit_guard.py -q -p no:cacheprovider
All must pass. Reply with only the final pytest summary line.
